← Object Storage Pricing Calculator

How to choose object storage by egress

Put your GB stored, GB egress per month and growth rate into the calculator to price Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, DigitalOcean Spaces and Hetzner Object Storage side by side. These are the questions to settle before you trust the answer.

Why does the same data cost so differently across object-storage providers?

Hyperscalers such as Amazon S3 charge a low-looking per-GB storage rate and then bill every GB you download at several cents, so serving data can cost many times what storing it does. Cloudflare R2 charges nothing for egress, Backblaze B2 and Wasabi bundle free egress up to a multiple of what you store, and Spaces and Hetzner sell a flat base fee with storage and transfer included. At 5 TB stored and 8 TB served a month, the cheapest and most expensive list prices in the calculator differ by roughly $800 a month.

What matters more than the per-GB price?

Your access pattern. Egress-heavy workloads (public downloads, video, model weights, backups restored often) favour zero-egress or bundled-egress providers, while rarely-read archives favour the lowest storage rate. Request fees, minimum retention, and where your compute runs also matter: moving data out of S3 to a compute provider elsewhere is itself egress.

When should I move to a different provider?

When the 12-month spend under your growth rate differs enough to pay for the migration: copying the data out (which is egress from the old provider), changing endpoints and credentials, and checking S3-API compatibility for the features you use such as presigned URLs, lifecycle rules and versioning. Run the calculator with your own volumes and growth before deciding.

Enter the GB you store, the GB you serve per month and your growth rate. Get Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, DigitalOcean Spaces and Hetzner priced side by side, the 12-month spend, and the egress level where the cheapest provider changes — before you build on one and find out when the invoice arrives.

Prefer a CLI, or want a budget gate in CI?

node cli.mjs compare --stored-gb 5000 --egress-gb 8000 --growth 5
node cli.mjs compare --stored-gb 5000 --egress-gb 8000 --provider s3 --budget 300   # exit 1 over budget
node cli.mjs crossover --stored-gb 2000

Get cli.mjs and engine.mjs — Node 18+, nothing to install, no network call. More: how to choose object storage by egress.

Common questions

Does this read my storage account?

No. It uses only the stored and egress volumes (GB) you type and rate cards you can edit. It cannot see your buckets, regions, request counts or invoice. Treat every figure as a way to compare options, never as what you will be charged.

Where do the prices come from?

They are approximate public list prices as best known in 2025 for each provider's main US or EU region, shown with an as-of line, and every number is editable. Providers change packaging often, so check each pricing page before deciding.

What is not included?

Request and operation fees (PUT, GET, LIST), minimum object-retention and early-deletion charges, replication, other regions, support plans, committed-use discounts and each provider's fair-use terms. Request fees can dominate for many small objects, and Wasabi, Backblaze and others limit free egress to a ratio of what you store, so check the terms against your access pattern. Use this to compare the storage and egress lines, not to forecast the whole invoice.

Is my data uploaded anywhere?

No. The page calculates in your browser and sends nothing. The CLI reads local files and makes no network call.
